segments.t: I'm here in Washington, D.C. on really a beautiful fall morning with Fed Governor Chris Waller.
Governor Waller, thanks for joining us.
Well, thanks for having me on, Steve.
Let's, I think, start where everybody wants to know, which is your views on inflation.
The last couple reports have come in somewhat hot.
Does it change your view of the outlook for inflation?
Yeah, I mean, I'm very concerned about inflation.
It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out.
It's not just concentrated in a few categories.
And that, as Chairman Waters said in his Jackson Hole speech,
that's one of the concerns is when inflation starts spreading out,
and it's not just a one-time level shock or something else.
So that's got me really concerned about inflation,
and so I think we need to get a lot more –
I mean, inflation's been above our target for over five years.
So if you really want to get it down, you've got to start taking more aggressive actions.
There was a metric that Chairman Waters used, I believe it was Jackson Hole,
where we talked about the percentage of items in the basket that were rising more than 3 percent.
Have you updated that number, and what is your evidence that it's broadening?
Well, we looked at CPI, and for, like, you know, core services,
like 70 percent of those goods are now over 3 percent.
And that's roughly 55, I think don't remember the exact number,
but roughly 50 to 55 percent of the CPI.
So – and that's not affected by tariffs.
That's not affected by oil.
So you've got a lot of things that are unaffected by these one-off shocks
that we're now seeing inflation going above 3 percent.
What's your thinking about why that the inflation is affecting services?
You know, some of this is just going to be the fact that I think firms can –
it's been at 3 percent.
I mean, increasingly, you're not going to see it in maybe market expectations,
but firms are thinking consumers are resilient, they'll pay,
and we can pass through with 3 percent increases or higher.
You're starting to hear – we're starting to hear some of that.
I heard it just last week talking to somebody,
man, we put through 3 percent because we think we can get it.
And that's when you start having problems of trying to get it.
